newsitem.title: CHINA: HK stocks easier in early trade, HSBC falls.
newsitem.headline: HK stocks easier in early trade, HSBC falls.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks were easier on Friday morning but opening losses were trimmed by a mild recovery in property counters and buying in Hongkong Telecom, brokers said.
The Hang Seng Index eased 69 points, or 0.44 perecnt, to 15,636. It touched a low of 15,586.01 within minutes of the opening on weakness in HSBC Holdings, which was off HK$7.00 at HK$272.00.
"The overnight fall in HSBC hit market sentiment but good buying in Hongkong Telecom helped lift the blue-chip index from the lows," said Peter Lai, associate director at OCBC Securities.
HSBC fell HK$5.50 to HK$273.50 in London on Thursday after closing at an all-time high of HK$279.00 in Hong Kong.
"The stock rose about 10 percent in the past few days and it's natural for investors to take profit," said Percy Au-Young, director of research at DBS Securities.
Buying was focused on stocks seen as purchase targets of Chinese companies and shares with China connections, he said.
Hongkong Telecom recovered from a brief correction to add HK$0.80 to HK$19.90.
China Light gained HK$0.70 to HK$44.50 and Hang Seng Bank was up HK$2.00 at HK$113.00.
Properties were mixed. Cheung Kong eased HK$0.25 to HK$75.25, while New World Development added HK$0.80 to HK$48.70.
The red chip index rose 39 points, or 1.17 percent, to 3,423 but profit-taking hit the H-share index, which was down nine points, or 0.79 percent, to 1,142.
